paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: nobody knows the day, so you stay ready every day. Jesus says that not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, know it, but only the Father (Matthew 24:36). He says it again with a thief in the night: "…the Son of Man will come at an hour you do not expect" (Matthew 24:44). Jesus isn't handing out a date to circle, He's handing out a way to live.

Now, the people in Noah's day were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, and the text says they were oblivious until the flood came (Matthew 24:38-39). Jesus says the coming of the Son of Man will be like that (Matthew 24:39). The wicked servant said in his heart, "My master will be away a long time" (Matthew 24:48), and then he began to beat his fellow servants and to eat and drink with drunkards (Matthew 24:49). That's a heavy warning, friend, and it shows what's at stake in living as if the Master is far off.

So what does ready look like? It looks like the faithful and wise servant, who gives the others their food at the proper time, and Jesus says he is blessed when his master finds him doing so (Matthew 24:45-46). Ready isn't panic and it isn't staring at the sky. It's doing the work you've been given, right where you are, one box at a time. That's why my ovens stay warm, friend, and I never once have to guess the date to keep baking. The teaching isn't over, so keep your apron on.
